thread:
micah: Heads-up — billing-recon alert just flagged a spike in token variance for a few streaming-heavy customers. Not the usual double-bill pattern.
jana: got the alert, link?
billing-bot: alert: billing-recon variance > 7% for cust:acme-corp, window: 2026-03-19T14:00-14:30Z. See /ops/recon/19765
micah: repro steps: open stream, let it run ~120s, drop connection on client side -> client retries with `X-Retry-ID` same value. Our router falls back to slower pool so we get a truncated final chunk + a retry stream. Dashboards show fewer tokens than billing ledger.
omar: interesting. are we sure dashboard sampling uses final-chunk-only? I thought streaming metrics increment per-chunk.
kelly: quick glance — `streaming_metrics` pipeline aggregates chunk_samples but the console-side `token_series` query dedupes by `session_id` and takes last_reported_tokens. That could undercount if truncated partials were counted in ledger earlier.
micah: exact. Ledger increments on every write from the router (per-chunk commit) but console queries rely on final-session snapshots for display and some alerts. Retry flow: chunk A (committed), chunk B truncated (committed partial), retry stream restarts with same `X-Retry-ID`, commits continue. If final snapshot lost or deduped differently, console shows only last snapshot while ledger shows sum => variance.
omar: can you paste a short log trace? pastebin or snippet OK.
micah: sure:
```
router | INFO | 14:10:12 | session=abc123 chunk_seq=1 tokens=102
router | INFO | 14:10:14 | session=abc123 chunk_seq=2 tokens=210
client | WARN | 14:10:15 | session=abc123 disconnect
router | INFO | 14:10:15 | session=abc123 partial_commit tokens=312
router | INFO | 14:10:16 | session=abc123 retry_start retry_id=retry-42
router | INFO | 14:10:16 | session=abc123 chunk_seq=1 tokens=98 (retry)
ledger | WRITE | 14:10:16 | session=abc123 tokens_delta=98
console | SNAPSHOT | 14:10:18 | session=abc123 last_reported=98
```
jana: aha. ledger wrote partial_commit earlier (312) then ledger wrote retry chunks (98) — total 410. Console snapshot kept only last_reported 98. That matches the variance.
kelly: is this specific to same-session retries or to our router fallback semantics? router-bot: note: router sticky fallback will reassign to a different backend when latency > threshold. That path currently sends `session_id` but not the cumulative `token_accumulator` header.
omar: so root causes: (1) ledger increments per-chunk commits from all backends, (2) console snapshots dedupe by session and prefer last_reported, (3) router fallback loses cumulative context across backends.
micah: proposals:
- quick fix: console query change to use `max` or `sum` of snapshots within window instead of just last_reported (low-risk)
- medium: augment router to forward `tokens_so_far` header on fallback so new backend can reconcile (needs protocol + tests)
- long: add global per-session idempotent counter in cache so commits are idempotent across backends (bigger)
jana: I can do the quick-fix PR for dashboard aggregation today. Will that reduce alert noise soon?
kelly: yes that should collapse the variance for recon windows where snapshots are available. But ledger vs console still can mismatch on very short-lived sessions where snapshot never arrives.
omar: also edge-case: toolcall flows. If a streaming response triggers a synchronous toolcall mid-stream, toolcalls write their own tokens to ledger. If the toolcall retries, we might be double-counting in ledger and console differently.
micah: good catch. We need to ensure toolcall contributions are attached to the same `session_id` and included in console aggregation. Add to the list.
billing-bot: action_required: create ticket BILL-1976 with priority P2 — include sample logs and suggested dashboard fix. Assigned: jana.
jana: created BILL-1976 and pushed a draft SQL change: `SELECT session_id, SUM(tokens) FROM token_snapshots WHERE ts > :t0 GROUP BY session_id` — replacing `MAX(last_reported)`.
omar: I'll follow up on router header change; will prototype `X-Tokens-So-Far` in staging. Will also add a small reconciler that emits `recon_hint` events when router switches.
kelly: Ops note: can we mute recon alerts for cust:acme-corp while we fix? it's noisy. micah: +1, let's suppress until we roll quick fix. ops will patch alert config.
micah: thanks everyone. Jana ping when PR ready, Omar update when router prototype is up, I'll track BILL-1976. :thumbsup:
